items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

ctx.x: the forties up, the real standards. They’re just songs, written by songwriters before the musicians started writing songs. Not that musicians wrote bad songs but you know you had the Lerner and Loewe and all the other ones, they were all great songwriters.
That’s an interesting point you just made. The classic, the standards that never seem to die, like Rod Stewart can—
